source: Neuropeptide Y and neuron-specific enolase levels in benign and malignant pheochromocytomas. Neuropeptide Y (NPY) is a newly identified peptide in the peripheral and central nervous systems. Blood NSE and plasma NPY concentrations have been reported to be increased in some patients with pheochromocytoma. The authors examined whether measuring these molecules could help differentiate between benign and malignant forms of pheochromocytoma. NSE levels were usual in all patients with benign pheochromocytoma (n = 13) and increased in half of patients with malignant pheochromocytoma (n = 13). However, there was no difference in the fraction of patients with elevated NPY levels. These results show that the determination of serum NSE can be relevant to distinguish malignant and benign pheochromocytomas; measuring plasma NPY is not useful in differentiating the two types of tumors.

source: Sexually transmitted afflictions of the colon, rectum and anus. The problem of the 90s. The last two decades have seen a dramatic increase in the prevalence and types of sexually transmitted diseases. Up to 55 percent of gay men with anorectal disorders have gonorrhea; 80 percent of syphilis patients are homosexuals. Additionally, a variety of parasites, bacterial, viral, and protozoan, all plague the homosexual population. Additionally, the global AIDS epidemic has produced a multitude of colorectal manifestations. Acute cytomegalovirus ileocolitis is the most common reason for emergency abdominal surgery in gay men with AIDS. In addition to cryptosporidia and isospora, the individual may present to the colorectal surgeon with bloody diarrhea and weight loss before diagnosis of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease. Other patients may have Kaposi's colorectal sarcoma or anorectal lymphoma and will therefore be HIV positive. however, in addition to these various manifestations, a third of AIDS patients consult the colorectal surgeon either for condyloma acuminatum, or for anorectal septicemia, or for proctitis before the diagnosis of HIV disease. Although intense anorectal surgery is associated with reasonable surgical outcomes in some asymptomatic HIV-positive patients, the same procedures in AIDS patients (symptomatic HIV-positive) will often produce disastrous results. source: Pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty in the management of thrombosed hemodialysis grafts: early and late clinical results. Pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty outcomes of 121 thrombosed hemodialysis grafts were reviewed. The initial pharmacomechanical method (used in 65 cases) used maceration of the clot with hook-shaped catheters and lacing of the clot with highly concentrated urokinase. The current technique (used in 56 cases) consisted of a pulsed spray injection of urokinase into the clot. All completely treated grafts (117 cases) underwent complete or near-complete thrombolysis, and 93% remained patent after 1 day. The average pulse spray lysis time was 46 minutes +/- 21. One patient (less than 1%) had a gastrointestinal hemorrhage and received a transfusion; minor complications occurred in 3% of patients. The primary and secondary graft patency rates for the two methods at 1 year were 26% and 51%, respectively. Although graft age and angioplasty results did not influence future graft patency, shorter intervals between graft thromboses were indicative of subsequent subsequent graft failure. The results suggest that pharmacomechanical thrombolysis and angioplasty provide rapid, consistent, and safe recanilization of thrombized hemodialysis grafts and represent a promising additional therapeutic approach for long-term graft management.

Color Doppler analysis of mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation: usefulness of the flow convergence region proximal to the regurgitant orifice.  
In prosthetic or paravalvular mitral regurgitation, transthoracic color Doppler flow imaging may occasionally fail to identify the regurgitant jet in the left atrium due to the shadow of the artificial valve.  
To overcome this constraint, we examined the utility of color Doppler imaging of the flow convergence region (FCR) proximal to the regurgitant orifice in 20 consecutive patients with mechanical prosthetic mitral regurgitation documented by surgery and cardiac catheterization (13 of 20 patients).  
Additionally, we analyzed 33 patients with normally functioning mitral implants.  
Doppler examinations were performed in the apical, subcostal, and parasternal long axis planes.  
FCR was identified in 95% (19 of 20) of patients with prosthetic mitral regurgitation.

Sodium-sensitive hypertension and sodium conservation.  
The differences between sodium-sensitive and sodium-sensitive hypertension have been theoretically studied using a water reservoir model of regulation of body fluid volume and blood pressure.  
If an outlet valve is installed on a tank whose base area is equal to the reciprocal of the total peripheral resistance (TPR) and water is introduced into that tank at a rate equivalent to the amount of Na+ absorbed, then equilibrium must be achieved at a certain water level, volume, and flow rate of the outlet, which represent mean arterial pressure (MAP), cardiac output (CO), and urinary excretion of Na+.  
The height of the outlet from the bottom of the reservoir and the magnitude of the outlet cross-section correspond to the intercept and slope of the renal function (pressure-natriuresis) curve, respectively.  
In sodium-non-sensitive hypertension, due to the shift of the curve to a higher blood pressure level (marked height of the outflow) without change in the slope (output magnitude), and in sodium-sensitive hypertension, due to the decreased slope of the curve (reduced outflow magnitude), not only the MAP (water level) but also the CO (water volume) are increased, resulting in sodium-conserving hypertension, if the TPR (inverse baseline surface area) remains unchanged, while CO is somewhat unchanged, resulting in non-sodium hypertension.  
Maintain hypertension, if TPR is elevated.  
Thus, MAP and its responsiveness to sodium intake are determined by the renal function curve.  
Since body fluid volume is set by both the renal function curve and the TPR, changes in TPR during the emergence of hypertension are a major factor in determining whether or not body fluid volume should change only a small amount or a large amount.  
Therefore, sodium responsiveness of blood pressure and sodium conservation must be considered separately.

source: Perforation of the gallbladder: comparison of cholescintigraphic and ultrasound results with the Niemeier classification. source: In vitro and in vivo effects in the coronary sinus of non-arc and arc shocks using an innovative low-power DC ablation system. DC shocks within the coronary sinus have been removed due to the danger of cardiac rupture and tamponade. Catheter ablation using DC energy on electrodes straddling the coronary sinus ostium, when employed clinically, has been reported to result in cardiac tamponade in up to 16% of patients. An innovative energy distribution system optimizes tension while reducing the undesirable effects caused by barotrauma. This system includes 1) a low-energy ablation power supply with a short, time-stable capacitive discharge that delivers up to 40J and 3000V and 2) a low-energy ablation catheter with a contoured distal electrode. We carried out in vitro and in vivo studies of this innovative system and evaluated shocks with arc and shocks without arc. Ablations were performed using unipolar distal shocks (D) and unipolar shocks to both electrodes made electrically identical (P-D). In vitro studies were conducted in a large tank filled with physiological saline while recording voltage, current, and pressure. High-speed cinematography (32,000 frames/sec) of shocks from 10 to 40J allowed detailed analysis of the vapor globe. Anodal shocks less than 20J showed no arcing or only negligible vapor glob formation. For the 40J D and P‑D anodal shocks, the vapor globe diameters were 31 and 22mm, respectively, associated with pressure recordings of 11 and 4.9atm. The pressure build-up lasted less than 50µs. The in vivo studies involved 18 dogs having undergone shocks without an arc (one to six shocks of 15J) and 18 dogs having undergone shocks with an arc (one to three shocks of 40J). Each group was segmented into D and P‑D shocks; Catheter ablation was performed at a mean distance +/- SEM of 2.94 +/- 0.92cm in the coronary sinus. All dogs accepted the procedure without cardiac rupture or tamponade. When killed 2 to 4 days later, the dogs showed edema and hyperemia or hemorrhage in the coronary sinus. To further explore the mechanism of glucose intolerance and insulin resistance detected in patients with fibrosis and portal hypertension, we studied a 35-year-old woman with presinusoidal portal hypertension without fibrosis due to nodular regenerative hyperplasia of the liver. source: The metabolic consequences of “flushed” cardiopulmonary bypass pump priming fluid in children undergoing cardiac operations. The amount of pump priming fluid substrate, particularly glucose and lactate, has a major impact on the metabolic response of children during cardiac operations and can be neurologically damaging. It is possible to purify the priming fluid from these excess substrates by ultrafiltration followed by the addition of a harmonized electrolyte solution. We applied this technique in the bypass management of nine children over 1 year old and weighing less than 18 kg who were studied from induction of anesthesia until 6 hours postoperatively. Regular blood samples were taken to measure electrolytes, intermediate metabolites and stress-related hormones. Throughout the study period, electrolyte concentrations were kept within normal limits and variations in blood glucose and lactate were minimized compared to those in matched historical controls from previous studies. During the cardiopulmonary bypass period, mean serum glucose concentrations ranged from 4.4 to 7.7 mmol/L and peaked at 10.7 mmol/L just before skin closure. The average serum lactate concentration did not exceed 2.3 mmol/L during the study period. Thus, ultrafiltration of the priming fluid and its substitution with a harmonized electrolyte solution results in the administration of a physiologically adequate substrate load to the patient, which is reflected in optimized control of average concentrations of intermediate metabolites in plasma. The method could serve as a basis for further clinical studies aimed at determining specific aspects of the metabolic response to stress in children.

source: Excess reperfusion of cardioplegic blood solution. A preventable factor of post-ischemic myocardial depression. Reperfusion of warm cardioplegic blood solution is beneficial in attenuating reperfusion damage after ischemia. This study examines the hypothesis that too early administration of cardioplegic blood solution during reperfusion counteracts these benefits and may result in a frequency of impaired ventricular performance and mortality comparable to that observed after normal blood reperfusion. Thirty-one dogs underwent global ischemia at 37°C for 45 minutes on a ventilated bypass. Six were provided with standard blood reperfusion and 25 were provided with warm cardioplegic blood solution fortified with aspartate/glutamate; among them, eight received a large dose (3,600 +/- 600 ml) and 17 received cardioplegic blood reperfusion at a restricted dose (1,180 +/- 120 ml) during a period of 10 to 20 minutes. High-dose cardioplegic blood perfusion (5,100 +/- 200 ml) without prior ischemia was tested in five additional dogs. High-dose blood cardioplegia without prior ischemia did not alter ventricular function (stroke peak work index 96% of control). After ischemia, standard blood reperfusion (absence of cardioplegia) resulted in significant left ventricular dysfunction (peak stroke work index 36% of control, p less than 0.05 compared to control) and a mortality rate of 33% (2/6 died). High-dose reperfusion resulted in modest recovery of stroke work index (40% of control, p less than 0.05 vs. control) and a mortality rate of 25% (2/8 died). In contrast, reperfusion with a restricted dose of cardioplegic blood solution ensured 100% survival (17/17) and restored the stroke work index to 90% of control (1.3 versus 1.45 gm.m/kg). We infer that reperfusion damage can be avoided by initial reoxygenation with moderate doses of substrate-enriched cardioplegic blood solution. Conversely, high-dose reperfusion of cardioplegic blood solution eliminates this benefit, results in significantly reduced recovery, and can be fatal.

source: Family convalescence after vascular surgery. Twenty-one families were observed during a 3-month study to assess families' ability to cope with major vascular surgery and recovery. Containment refers to an aggregate of constructed meanings for events and behavioral responses used by families to regulate the impact of the surgical crisis and decrease family disruption. This “confined” coping pattern was expressed in families' avoidant behaviors and restricted definitions of the problem: that is, they framed their situation in terms of surgical repair as a cure rather than a palliative intervention for a chronic, progressive illness. source: Strawberry hemangiomas, or capillaries, are common vascular tumors, with an incidence of approximately 2.6% in newborns. Treatments such as cryosurgery, irradiation, radium instillation, corticosteroid therapy or surgical excision are sometimes ineffective or cause significant morbidity. Patients received 3.1 +/- 1 (mean +/- SD) laser treatments, with a mean lesion regression of 69.9% +/- 4.5%. There was no evidence of hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation. source: Effects of MK-801 on restoration of sensorimotor cortex lesions. Histological evidence indicates that substances acting as non-competitive inhibitors of the N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor may have beneficial or negative effects on neurons of the central nervous system. In the present studies, we investigated the effects of MK-801 on the restoration of behavioral activity after unilateral lesions in the rat somatic sensorimotor cortex. In the first study, rats with unilateral damage to the sensorimotor cortex received either MK-801 (1 mg/kg) or saline 12 to 16 hours after surgery. Additional injections were administered on postoperative days 2, 4, and 6. Behavioral tests assessed somatosensory asymmetries (i.e., bilateral tactile stimulation tests) and forelimb position. After induction of sensorimotor cortex lesions, rats showed an ipsilateral somatosensory bias and impairment in contralateral forelimb stance. Rats administered with MK-801 recovered slightly faster than animals administered with saline, as determined by a bilateral tactile stimulation test (p less than 0.05). In contrast, there was no marked difference between groups in restoring forelimb stance. In a second study, rats with damage to the sensorimotor cortex were treated with a single injection of MK-801 after behavioral restoration. Twenty hours after MK-801 injection, rats with sensorimotor cortex lesions showed restoration of placement deficits. The withdrawal persisted for at least 7 days after the injection. These behavioral data support the idea that MK-801 may have beneficial or adverse effects when administered after brain injury.

source: The relevance of cytogenetic research in adult acute lymphocytic leukemia. OBJECTIVE: The prognostic significance of pretreatment marrow cytogenetic analyzes in adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia treated at a single institution, with an identical treatment program, is described. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 105 patients developing a documented morphological diagnosis of acute lymphocytic leukemia were examined for this analysis. All patients underwent a thorough workup at presentation and chromosomal analysis was performed in 103 patients, using the Giemsa strip method with trypsin preparation on cells in 24-hour culture. RESULTS: The specific cytogenetic classification in the 103 patients who underwent karyotypic analysis was as follows: diploid 27%; Philadelphia chromosome positive 13%; hyperdiploid 12%; B cell karyotype 6%; 6q- and 14q+ anomalies 4%; pseudodiploid 8%; hypodiploid 2%; and incomplete metaphases 28%. B-cell, 6q- or 14q+, and Philadelphia chromosome-positive karyotypes tend to be related to other known negative prognostic factors. Patients developing diploid, hyperdiploid, pseudodiploid and hypodiploid karyotypes or with incomplete metaphases could be grouped into a single group with an advantageous prognosis. In this group, the remission rate after induction chemotherapy was 89%, the median duration of total remission was 26 months, and the median survival was 25 months, with a 3-year survival rate of 45%. Patients with Philadelphia chromosome-positive, B-cell, and 6q- or 14q+ abnormalities collectively had a poor prognosis. Their response rate to induction chemotherapy was 65%, the median duration of response was 7 months, and the median survival was 8 months, with a 3-year survival rate less than 10%. CONCLUSION: We conclude that pretreatment marrow karyotype is a crucial part of the evaluation of adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia and provides relevant data.

source: Smooth muscle cell growth and restenosis after independent coronary angioplasty with excimer laser. It has been shown that excimer laser coronary angioplasty can remove atherosclerotic intracoronary tissue. Standalone excimer laser coronary angioplasty was successfully performed in a 53-year-old white man with 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending coronary artery and exertional angina (Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III). The lesion was lowered to 30% residual stenosis using a 1.2 mm and then 1.8 mm diameter laser catheter. Early follow-up angiography, 24 hours later, revealed continued patency and unchanged lesion diameter of the target vessel. The patient was symptom free during the 2-month follow-up period, but died suddenly while playing in a tennis tournament 63 days after surgery. Autopsy histological examination revealed 80% restenosis at the lesion site without plaque rupture or thrombosis. Specific staining of the histological specimen for smooth muscle cells using alpha-actin revealed marked proliferation of smooth muscle cells at the site of excimer laser coronary angioplasty. However, the majority of vessel narrowing appeared to be due to underlying fibrous plaque resulting from insufficient tissue ablation. This was likely related to the size of currently available catheters, which are too small to create a large channel.

source: Late consequences of treatment for Wilms tumor. An article from the National Wilms Tumor Study Group. The National Wilms' Tumor Study (NWTS) was inaugurated in 1969. One of its objectives was to adjust treatments according to risk factors in order to reduce the number and severity of short- and long-term iatrogenic complications linked to treatment. The NWTS therefore included a long-term follow-up study (LTFS) as part of its framework to observe late effects. The LTFS is restricted to relapse-free survivors living 5 years or more after initial surgery, and data are collected using specially designed forms. A total of 787 patients enrolled in NWTS-1 or NWTS-2 (1969 to 1979) were eligible, of whom 680 (86%) were accessible for analysis regarding their musculoskeletal, cardiac, and neuropsychological status, as well as the presence of benign and malignant tumors. Patients with early-stage disease treated with radiation therapy developed scoliosis, along with other musculoskeletal abnormalities (32 versus 2), almost seven times more frequently than members of the cohort population who did not receive radiation therapy (35 of 57 versus 5 of 53, respectively). The difference in cardiovascular complications noted among survivors who did or did not receive Adriamycin (Adria Laboratories, Columbus, OH) (2.4 versus 1.1 per 100 person-years at risk) had limited statistical significance (P = 0.06). No excess neuropsychological events were reported in people who received the nerve agent vincristine. When considering patients with disease at all stages, all five malignancies occurred in all 623 patients who underwent radiotherapy (RT patients); benign tumors were also more common in RT patients than in patients who did not receive radiotherapy (41 of 486 or 8% versus 4 of 194 or 2%). Perpetual study of this unique body of patients is necessary, particularly for those receiving Adriamycin, due to the known harsh interval required for latent cardiomyopathy to manifest clinically in some patients.

source: Evaluation of oral hairy leukoplakia by ultrastructural examination of exfoliative cytological samples. Lingual exfoliative cytology samples (scrapings) were collected from 18 human immunodeficiency virus-positive patients with clinical oral hairy leukoplakia. Scrapings of the oral mucosa were performed in 12 of these patients. The specimens were subjected to transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis. Sixteen (89%) of the lingual samples revealed infection of keratinocytes with a herpes-like virus. There was no evidence of viral infection among the 12 oral mucosa scrapings. Fungal hyphae were observed by TEM in 14 (78%) of the lingual scrapings and two (17%) of the oral scrapings. One exfoliation sample and two biopsy samples were stained for Epstein-Barr virus DNA using a DNA probe. Visualization of herpetic virions by TEM in the keratinocytes of a lesion clinically suspected of being hairy leukoplakia ensures a direct and objective diagnosis. Furthermore, the use of exfoliative cytological samples represents a clinically simple and non-invasive method.
